slot.brief: A circular loop of changing radius in a uniform magnetic field; ask for the induced emf as a function of time via dΦ/dt (no figure needed).

stem: A circular loop lies in a plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T. The radius of the loop changes with time as r = (2 + 0.5*t) m. The magnitude of the induced emf in the loop as a function of time is
working:
r = 2 + 0.5t, so dr/dt = 0.5 m/s. Phi = B*pi*r^2. e = dPhi/dt = B*2*pi*r*(dr/dt) = 0.2*2*pi*(2+0.5t)*0.5 = 0.1*pi*(t+4) V.

Independent check: \(\mathcal{E}=B\left|d(\pi r^2)/dt\right|=2\pi B r\,dr/dt=0.2\pi(2+0.5t)=0.1\pi(t+4)\,\text{V}.
solution:
Magnetic flux is $Phi=B\pi r^2$, so the induced emf magnitude is
$$\mathcal{E}=\left|\frac{d\Phi}{dt}\right|=2\pi Br\frac{dr}{dt}.$$
Substituting $B=0.2\,\text{T}$, $r=2+0.5t$ and $dr/dt=0.5\,\text{m s}^{-1}$ gives $\mathcal{E}=0.1\pi(t+4)\,\text{V}$.
